Bill.BriefDescription: Creating and using digital infrastructure maps to inform economic development decisions.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to creating and using digital infrastructure mapsto inform economic development decisions; amending RCW 43.330.010; andadding new sections to chapter 43.330 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.330 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The legislature finds that every year significant public andprivate infrastructure investments are made in Washington for thepurposes of energy, information networks, water, sewer, andtransportation. These investments are critical to connecting regions,and to achieving longterm global competitiveness and to creating equalaccess to economic opportunity for all the state's citizens. (2) The legislature further finds that the public and privateinvestments may not be coordinated such that they provide maximumefficiency and effectiveness, and that access to a broader array ofinformation would enable the state to make and manage more informedinvestment decisions. (3) Therefore, the legislature intends to direct the use of p. 1 SHB 1819available maps and available data for the creation and use of digitalcrosssystem infrastructure maps to inform and develop state prioritiesaround economic development.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 43.330 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The state energy office and broadband office of the department,the public works board, and the community economic revitalizationboard, in collaboration with the department of transportation anddepartment of natural resources, and in consultation with otheragencies and organizations with expertise in energy, informationnetworks, water, sewer, and transportation, must: (a) Develop one or more digital layered maps that identify: (i) Major power facilities and energy infrastructure sites; (ii) Broadband availability; (iii) Water and sewer infrastructure; and (iv) Rail corridors, public highways including waterways, andports; and (b) Leverage and use available maps, available data, Washington'sadopted geographic information systems mapping standards, enterpriseinfrastructure, web services, and applications, where appropriate. (2) The department and department of transportation must analyzethe maps to identify: (a) Gaps in infrastructure, including missing, aged and substandardinfrastructure, corresponding with economic corridors; and (b) Priority areas for future investment, based on the ability ofthe infrastructure to meet the needs of local economies to compete inthe regional and global marketplace. (3) The department and department of transportation must jointlyreport to the legislature by January 1st of each year, beginning onJanuary 1, 2014, with the infrastructure gaps and investmentrecommendations.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 43.330.010 and 2011 c 286 s 4 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Unless the context clearly requires otherwise, the definitions inthis section apply throughout this chapter. SHB 1819 p. 2 (1) "Associate development organization" means a local economicdevelopment nonprofit corporation that is broadly representative ofcommunity interests. (2) "Department" means the department of commerce. (3) "Director" means the director of the department of commerce. (4) "Energy" has the definition in RCW 43.21F.025. (5) "Financial institution" means a bank, trust company, mutualsavings bank, savings and loan association, or credit union authorizedto do business in this state under state or federal law. (((5))) (6) "Microenterprise development organization" means acommunity development corporation, a nonprofit developmentorganization, a nonprofit social services organization or other locallyoperated nonprofit entity that provides services to lowincomeentrepreneurs. (((6))) (7) "Small business" has the same meaning as provided inRCW 39.29.006. (((7))) (8) "Statewide microenterprise association" means anonprofit entity with microenterprise development organizations asmembers that serves as an intermediary between the department ofcommerce and local microenterprise development organizations.
